title: Minimal Hostable Endpoints PRD — phased acceptance and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Ship a tightly scoped, production-safe minimal bundle of hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) that covers 80% of customer onboarding patterns while minimizing cross-team dependencies. This PRD defines the API surface, behavioral guarantees, telemetry, acceptance criteria, and a phased launch + rollback playbook to reduce blast radius.

Objectives:
- Deliver a minimal, stable surface for early adopters with clear contract and deterministic fallbacks.
- Ensure observable SLOs and cost guardrails for Hosted tier.
- Provide a documented rollback strategy and automated canary gating.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Multimodal input (image/audio) support.
- Advanced model selection heuristics beyond a single default and a lower-cost fallback.
- Deep SDK language parity; SDKs will route to the new surface but full client-feature parity tracked separately.

API surface (minimal):
- /v1/hosted/chat: streaming and non-streaming chat completions. Single default model alias (hosted-default-chat-v1). Optional system messages and function/tool-calling metadata support (subset).
- /v1/hosted/completions: single-turn text completion for short generation use cases.
- /v1/hosted/embeddings: high-throughput batch embeddings with max batch size gated by runtime.
- /v1/hosted/rerank: lightweight ranking endpoint accepting up to 50 candidates, return top-K with scores.

Behavioral contracts and limits:
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms for completions up to 128 tokens; chat p95 < 450ms for 256-token sessions in single-turn requests (streaming behavior excluded from strict latency SLO).
- Availability target: 99.9% for the hosted surface; critical errors >1% in 15m window trigger automatic traffic shift.
- Rate limits (initial): 100 requests/min per API key for chat/completions, 5000 embedding units/min per org by default. Billing and quota policies will be enforced server-side.
- Graceful degradation: when capacity constrained, system returns explicit HTTP 429 with retry-after and an advisory field "fallback_model" when a lower-cost compatible model is available.

Data & Security:
- Customer payloads are isolated; no cross-tenant KV cache leakage permitted.
- KMS-integrated logging for private tenants (flagged but not required in first cut).

Instrumentation & Observability requirements (gating):
- Per-route latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and error rates emitted to telemetry backend.
- Sampling for request/response traces (1 in 100 for full payloads) and 100% token-level cost accounting for billed requests.
- Alerting: p95 latency breach >5% for 30m, error rate >2% for 15m.

Launch plan (phased):
1) Internal canary (Week 0): route 1% of internal traffic and run e2e smoke tests; collect reliability/latency.
2) Early partners (Week 1): invite 5 beta customers with support on-call; route up to 5% live traffic.
3) Progressive ramp (Week 2-3): 5% -> 25% -> 50% based on gating signals.
4) General availability (Week 4): open sign-ups, enable default quotas.

Canary gating criteria (must pass to increase traffic):
- Rolling 24h p95 latency delta <= +15% vs baseline.
- Error rates <= 1% (non-429), customer visible failures <= 0.5%.
- No replication or cache isolation violations in scans.

Rollback playbook (automated + manual steps):
- Automated: if error-rate or latency gates are violated, traffic decreases by 50% every 5m until stable; after 3 reductions, automatic shift to fallback model/region and on-call alert.
- Manual: PM/Eng leads evaluate logs/dashboards, approve staged redeploy or full rollback. PRD owner initiates incident bridge if customer impact high.

Acceptance criteria (all items required for "Done"):
- API contract documented in the Console docs and OpenAPI spec published.
- End-to-end smoke tests (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) in CI with deterministic fixtures and golden outputs for template prompts.
- Load test demonstrating p95 SLO at 50% target traffic with production-like models.
- Telemetry pipelines ingest per-route metrics and alerts created in on-call pager.
- SDKs update sample snippets and test harnesses to call the new endpoints.
- Docs: quickstart, migration notes, and cost estimation guide published.

Quality checks and evals:
- Prompt set evaluation: quality baseline recorded against upstream model for a set of 250 representative prompts; regression threshold <= 5% for essential intents.
- Embedding cosine similarity baseline run against known dataset to ensure vector drift < 2%.

Dependencies (critical):
- ENG: runtime support for streaming and token accounting (ENG-3392).
- Infra: quota & billing enforcement (ENG-4120).
- Design: console onboarding flow & dashboard (DES-214).
- Legal: export control & data residency sign-off for EU regions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected token-cost spikes from aggressive default max_tokens. Mitigation: default conservative max_tokens and token-cost telemetry with rate-limit throttles.
- Risk: Customer confusion over behavioral differences between hosted-default-chat-v1 and fallback model. Mitigation: explicit response metadata and doc callouts.

Scope clarifications and change log:
- 2025-02-24: Reduced scope to single default model alias for each surface to avoid model orchestration delays (PM decision).
- 2025-02-28: Deferred SSO/KMS private-tenant integrations to follow-up ticket due to extended compliance timeline.
- 2025-03-03: Added rerank endpoint limit of 50 candidates after performance trade-off analysis.

Operational playbooks (links in links field) and runbook snippets are included below; runbook must be validated by infra on-call before go-live.

Owner & sign-offs:
- PRD owner: Aisha Kapoor (Product).
- Eng lead: Liam Chen.
- Design lead: Sofia Martinez.
- Security/compliance: Priya Nair.

Post-launch metrics (30/60/90d):
- Adoption: orgs using hosted endpoints and ratio of chat vs embeddings vs rerank.
- Economics: cost per 1k tokens and median cost delta vs baseline.
- Quality: evaluation regression rate and customer-reported issues.

Notes: Avoid aggressive feature expansion in the first 4 weeks; prioritize stability, clear docs, and retrievability of telemetry for rapid iteration.
